Tech Report: Saving Nepal’s wild orchids — in photos

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1098 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that prized for their ornamental and medicinal value, hundreds of orchids are illegally harvested and sold each year.
  • It has been revealed that A couple of hours drive from Kathmandu, in the hills near Chitlang village in central Nepal, a group of locals and forest officials gather in a dense subtropical woodland.
  • Bashyal refers to this team as a taskforce — one on the hunt for illegal activity.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that prized for their ornamental and medicinal value, hundreds of orchids are illegally harvested and sold each year. Now, conservationist Reshu Bashyal is leading an effort to protect them.

Words by Saugat Bolakhe and photos by CJ Karki.

It has been revealed that A couple of hours drive from Kathmandu, in the hills near Chitlang village in central Nepal, a group of locals and forest officials gather in a dense subtropical woodland. Beneath a canopy of pines, Himalayan chestnuts and Nepalese alders, the group listens as wildlife conservationist Reshu Bashyal guides them through a questionnaire designed to document the signs of poaching.

Bashyal refers to this team as a taskforce — one on the hunt for illegal activity. But instead of focusing on animals, as many conservation projects do, the group’s objective is to protect flora, specifically orchids. These flowering plants are harvested and sold across Nepal’s borders.

The flowers are prized for their ornamental value, but they are also used in traditional medicines, including Chinese, Tibetan and Ayurveda healing products.

It has been revealed that multiple parts of the plant, including the stem and fruit, can also be used as ingredients. “It’s as if these plants have some magical properties about them,” Bashyal says.

Nepal has more than 500 orchid species, many of which are heavily harvested. Between 2008 and 2016, the country legally exported more than 47,000 kilograms of wild-collected orchids. However, discrepancies exist between Nepal’s export data and those of its trading partners, arising from problems such as mismatched and unreported trade amounts and species being sold under different names.

Industry observers note that the trade in animal and plant species is regulated mostly under the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES) agreement, which is designed to protect wildlife from exploitation. Although Nepal joined the convention more than 50 years ago, it did not introduce legislation to implement CITES until 2017.

The orchid Dendrobium longicornu is sought after for its black-haired canes and fragrant white and orange blooms.

The orchid Dendrobium longicornu is sought after for its black-haired canes and fragrant white and orange blooms.

All but two species of orchid in Nepal are now listed in CITES Appendix II, which includes species that are not presently threatened with extinction but could be if their trade is not regulated. The government must create a management initiative and a formal assessment to confirm that harvesting a species for trade won’t harm the survival of the wild population. “We haven’t prepared such a management plan for any orchid species yet. So, their trade is still considered illegal here,” Bashyal adds. Violation of the CITES Act can lead to a fine of up to 100,000 Nepalese rupees (US$660), one year in prison, or both.

Bashyal started researching orchids in 2018, when conservation fieldwork revealed the extent of harvesting and trade of the plants.

Bashyal started researching orchids in 2018, when conservation fieldwork revealed the extent of harvesting and trade of the plants.

Bashyal demonstrates a survey technique to a member of her team.

Bashyal demonstrates a survey technique to a member of her team.

Bashyal (right) and a team from the non-profit organization Greenhood Nepal have partnered with forest officials and local community members to form an anti-poaching taskforce.

Bashyal (right) and a team from the non-profit organization Greenhood Nepal have partnered with forest officials and local community members to form an anti-poaching taskforce.

Sources indicate that bashyal first became involved in orchid research by chance. In 2018, while working on a conifer tree conservation project for non-profit organization Greenhood Nepal in Kathmandu, she visited several regional sites across the country and was often approached by people asking about the demand for orchids in the city. When her team investigated further, it realized that many people living in the villages were harvesting or actively trading the plants.

According to recent reports, this illegal trading was often overlooked by authorities, according to Bashyal. Before suggesting a way to stop it, the team had to understand the market — specifically which species were being taken, their conservation status and how the supply chain operated. To do this, it visited orchid trading hubs across Nepal and spoke to harvesters, traders and enforcement officials.

The Makawanpur region of Nepal is home to orchids, yew trees and a rich diversity of other wildlife.

The Makawanpur region of Nepal is home to orchids, yew trees and a rich diversity of other wildlife.

“The local people provide information on where orchids are harvested, moved, gathered and how much they sold orchids for,” she notes. During these visits, the team shared its research and spoke about the importance of conservation, which was well received, she says. “After all, an unsustainable harvesting of the orchids severely threatens local livelihood and income,” she adds.

Bashyal’s team at Greenhood Nepal learnt that several orchid species, including Satyrium nepalense and Pleione praecox, are harvested in large quantities for their medicinal value. Overharvesting an orchid species that is in decline can easily lead to its extinction in the wild, which makes understanding a species’ population and distribution crucial for creating sustainable harvesting practices.

After the field trips, Bashyal’s team created a series of policy briefs, drafted conservation frameworks and started the anti-poaching taskforce in collaboration with the region’s governmental forest management office to document illegal activity and conduct patrols.

Recent findings suggest that the team is also developing comprehensive identification manuals and guidelines for regulators. Many existing manuals focus on identifying whole plants and flowers, but traded items can include the orchid’s thickened stem and fleshy underground storage organs, called tubers. Some orchids are boiled, or dried for several hours or days before being traded.

Sources indicate that in some parts of Nepal, communities can earn a good income from harvesting and selling orchids alongside other medicinal plants. For many, medicinal plants are their sole source of income. “Simply telling the locals ‘you are not supposed to do this’ will not stop them from harvesting,” Bashyal states. For this reason, imposing a blanket ban on trade might not be effective.

Bashyal emphasizes that tracking the wildlife trade is complex and often requires navigating delicate legal territory. Researchers must also have patience when interviewing informants. “Thus, it also comes down to following research ethics, respect and treating local knowledge as a valuable resource to build trust,” Bashyal indicates. “Only after that, can we have data and develop any intervention.”.

The forests of Makawanpur support an array of native orchids.

The forests of Makawanpur support an array of native orchids.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, this blog is now closed. Read below for a roundup of headlines from and about Germany on the weekend of Saturday, November 21, and Sunday, November 22, 2026:.

Bosses at soccer team Bayern Munich have publicly questioned whether young Germany international Jamal Musiala's contract is valid in view of a debilitating neurological condition.

The remarks have been criticized by media and from several other quarters, among them the global players' union FIFPRO, which accused the officials of neglecting their "duty of care" toward their players.

You can read details on what has been happening at the top football club in this DW article: Bayern Munich bosses under fire over Jamal Musiala comments.

Friedrich Christian "Mick" Flick, an art collector, investor and multimillionaire who belonged to one of Germany's richest business dynasties, has died aged 82 in Rosenheim in the southern state of Bavaria, his family has noted.

The family said in a statement issued on Saturday that Flick left behind "the memory of a life shaped by significant acts of generosity as a donor and patron, particularly in contemporary art and in promoting tolerance.".

Flick was the grandson of Friedrich Flick, who made a huge fortune in the Nazi era with his coal and steel business, partly by using forced labor.

This past came back to haunt the grandson in 2003 when he pledged to loan his world-famous collection of modern art to Berlin, with the Central Council of Jews in Germany calling the Flick Collection a "Göring Collection" and saying the loan was intended to wash clean the "blood money" from the Nazi era.

The collection, which contains some 2,500 works by 150 artists, was exhibited in parts in the German capital from 2004 to 2021.

Flick later said in an interview that the widespread outrage, while hurtful, had forced him to look more closely at his family's history.

According to his family, Flick once said: "I have no guilt for my forefathers' conduct, but I feel a responsibility, a very special responsibility. Every German bears this responsibility. As a Flick, I bear it twice.".

Among other things, he collaborated with the Prussian Cultural Heritage Foundation, which oversees Berlin's museums, to research his family's Nazi past.

He also set up a foundation in Potsdam, near Berlin, that aimed to combat xenophobia and racism and contributed €5 million ($5.4 million) to the foundation to compensate former forced laborers.

The family was also involved in a highly publicized party donations scandal in the 1980s that became known as the "Flick Affair.".

According to recent reports, "Mick" Flick married Countess Maya von Schönburg (1958-2019), the older sister of well-known socialite, businesswoman, art collector and artist Gloria von Thurn und Taxis, in 1985. The couple had three children.

German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier is setting off on a five-day trip to Africa that will take him to Ivory Coast, Ghana and Kenya.

Steinmeier will be accompanied by a business delegation and is expected to focus on economic cooperation and the training of skilled workers during the trip.

On Monday, Steinmeier is to be received by Ivorian President Allassane Outtara in Abidjan, Ivory Coast's largest city and seat of government.

The next day, in the Ghanaian capital, Accra, he is set to open the German-African Business Summit, which, according to its website, "brings together senior business executives, policymakers, investors, and industry leaders from across Germany and Africa.".

On Wednesday, he will be received by Kenyan President William Ruto in Nairobi.

In Kenya, Steinmeier will also visit the Crescent Island Game Sanctuary on Thursday, the last day of his trip.

The Federal Institute for Hydrology (BfG) has said it expects water levels in large rivers in western Germany, including the Rhine, to return to average or above in the next few days amid sustained rainfall.

It noted the water level at the key gauge in Kaub near Koblenz, located at an vital bottleneck on the Middle Rhine, could reach some 3.3 meters (10.8 feet), more than 3 meters higher than the last recorded low-water readings.

The BfG said it also expected rising water levels in the Weser and Danube rivers, with smaller increases in the Elbe and Oder.

The rising water level in the Rhine, an important shipping route, means that conditions for water-borne cargo transport have improved, according to Germany's inland navigation association BDB.

"The more abundant rainfall in the past days has caused the water level in the Rhine to rise considerably, and they will keep rising a great deal in the next few days as well, meaning that each ship has much more transport capacity again," remarked Fabian Spiess, the deputy manager at BDB.

In the middle of the year, many ships were forced to drastically reduce the loads they carried, leading to economic losses that will not be recuperated any time soon, according to Spiess.

He cited the year 2018, in which shipping on the Rhine was also hindered by extremely low water levels, saying that the months of improved conditions at the end of that year had not been enough to make good the economic damage incurred.

The conservation NGO also noted that the current rain provided temporary relief to the environment but could not compensate for the negative consequences of the long dry period.

It said species of animals, such as amphibians and water insects, that lived in small bodies of water and moist habitats had been particularly impacted.

Justice Minister Stefanie Hubig claims that she intends to tighten the law on murders committed with "gender-specific" motives, with a particular focus on femicides perpetrated by men who are unable to accept a separation or the desire of a woman to live a self-determined life.

"A man kills, or attempts to kill, his partner or ex-partner almost every day in Germany," Hubig told the Sunday edition of the mass-circulation Bild newspaper.

Industry observers note that "Any man killing a woman because she wants to leave him must be punished as a murderer," she mentioned, noting that in some cases, courts cite a man's deep sadness or fear of losing a partner to someone else as extenuating circumstances. This can lead to a lesser conviction of manslaughter.

She noted that in future, courts should look more closely at such motives to determine whether they were based on sentiments of patriarchal possessiveness.

However, Hubig, who belongs to the center-left Social Democrats (SPD), remarked she was opposed to making femicide a separate category of crime, as some women's rights organizations have demanded.

She stated that, in her opinion, doing so would have "no advantages over what we are intending — and much bigger disadvantages.".

The proposals are right now being debated within the coalition government and are expected to be presented to the states and associations for consideration before the end of the year.

They will then have to go before the Cabinet before being put before the parliament.

The powerful IG Metall union said on Sunday it would call another 24-hour strike on Monday as a pay dispute continues.

Altogether, some 23,000 workers at 19 companies in northern Germany have been called upon to participate, including employees at automaker Mercedes-Benz, shipbuilding organization Meyer Werft and wind ​energy company Siemens Gamesa.

The union remarked that a strike on Friday saw some 12,300 workers walk out at 17 facilities.

It claims that the strikes are meant to increase the pressure on employers to yield to its demands, which include a 5% ‌wage increase.

So far, employers have ⁠offered a one-off payment next year and a 1.3% wage increase from July 2028.

The DW newsroom says "Willkommen!" once more to all its readers as we resume our reporting on all things German.

Some good news is on the agenda: The Rhine River, which we can see from the window of our Bonn office, has recovered after a long period with little rainfall, meaning that the barges plying the waterway can load up properly again.

In other stories, the German president, Frank-Walter Steinmeier, is setting off on a trip to Africa, during which he is set to visit three countries with a businesss delegation in tow.

And Germany's powerful IG Metall union has remarked it is launching another 24-hour strike on Monday amid an escalating pay dispute.

Read on to find out more about what is happening in Germany on Sunday, November 22.

We're pausing our Germany news blog for now. Come back for more on Sunday!

A new goal celebration was devised by Borussia Dortmund midfielder Felix Nmecha after his previous one caused controversy due to its religious aspect.

According to recent reports, after scoring the goal that secured Dortmund's 1-0 victory over Borussia Mönchengladbach (see entry below), Nmecha knelt on one knee and crossed his arms in front of his chest. He then spread his arms, appearing to pray with his eyes closed.

Nmecha told broadcaster Sky that he intends to continue expressing his faith during goal celebrations, adding that he had once again given glory to Jesus.

However, he did not perform the controversial part of his usual goal celebration. In it, he removes an imaginary crown from his head and places it on the pitch in front of him while kneeling.

This celebration has been heavily criticized, even by Dortmund's fan department.

Nmecha explained that the celebrations is about "putting down my 'crown' in front of the soon-to-come king and point out to Jesus, my hope and my strength.".

The gesture is used by Ballers in God, a network of Christian football players that has been criticized for the homophobic and queerphobic statements made by its members.

Dortmund president Hans-Joachim Watzke noted he asked the player not to do the celebration again.

Borussia Dortmund midfielder Felix Nmecha led his team to the top of the German Bundesliga table with a 1-0 victory over last-place Borussia Mönchengladbach.

According to recent reports, meanwhile, Bayern Munich was held to a 1-1 draw at home by Cologne on Friday, and striker Harry Kane suffered a serious ankle injury. The Ballon d'Or winner is set to miss several months after undergoing ankle surgery earlier on Saturday.

Now, Dortmund has 24 points after 10 games, putting them two points ahead of Bayern and third-place Freiburg, who defeated Elversberg 1-0.

Recent findings suggest that fourth-place RB Leipzig had five different players score in a 5-1 victory over Union Berlin, bringing them to 21 points. Bayer Leverkusen scored four unanswered goals against Paderborn to stay in fifth place.

Germany is seeking to redress years of underinvestment by pouring billions into the modernization of public infrastructure and digital networks, and the transition to renewable energy sources.

But will the initiative bring real change amid the labor shortages, burdensome bureaucracy and low productivity currently besetting Europe's largest economy?

DW takes a look at what is one of Germany's biggest public investment drives in decades in this video:.

Bundesliga powerhouse Bayern Munich concluded the 2025-26 financial year with record figures.

According to the financial report released Saturday at the club's annual general meeting, the club's total turnover was €988.2 million ($1.08 billion) — that is around €10 million more than the previous year.

Industry observers note that operating profit (EBITDA) increased from €187.8 million to €190.8 million. Pre-tax profit was €35.3 million, and net profit for the year was €22.8 million.

It has been revealed that bayern had a particularly strong year in terms of sponsorships. Turnover increased by nearly €30 million, reaching €268.4 million. The club also set a record in merchandise sales, earning €152.8 million.

Industry observers note that "We have achieved another record year," CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen stated. "This demonstrates that our club has a strong foundation. And we continue to invest to ensure the best possible conditions for the sporting success of our teams.".

Moreover, Bayern achieved another milestone. They reached 500,000 members — more than any other club in the world.

Over the past 12 years, the German giants have doubled their membership, growing from 250,000 in 2014 to 500,000 this year.

"Record champions, record members, record member champions," president Herbert Hainer mentioned.

Members hold a 70% stake in the club, which is well above the simple majority required by German rules.

The remaining 30% is owned by four German companies with roots in Bavaria: Adidas, Audi, Allianz, and Viessmann.

In a recent development, bayern won the league and cup double in the 2025-26 season, losing only three of 53 games across all competitions. In Europe, the club made it to the Champions League semifinals.

Two and a half weeks after his sudden death, Free Voters leader Hubert Aiwanger, who was Bavarian Minister of Economic Affairs and Deputy Minister-President, was laid to rest in his hometown of Inkofen in Lower Bavaria.

Industry observers note that A memorial service was held at the Parish Church of the Presentation of the Lord and broadcast on a screen outside. According to the organizers, around 2,000 people attended the solemn service.

It has been revealed that aiwanger's funeral was open to the public. His longtime partner, Tanja Schweiger, the Regensburg district administrator (Free Voters), stated that Aiwanger had been "a man of the people.".

For that reason, she noted, everyone "who liked and appreciated him" was warmly welcome. The politician had already been honored with a state funeral in Munich a week earlier.

It has been revealed that aiwanger was found dead in a Berlin hotel on November 4 after canceling an appointment for health reasons. The 55-year-old died of natural causes.

Harry Kane, Bayern Munich's star striker, has pledged to return to the field for the crucial matches at the end of the current campaign after undergoing surgery for a torn ankle ligament.

"I'll be back fresh and ready to go for the business end of the season," he wrote on social media above a photo of himself on his hospital bed, also thanking fans for their messages of support.

Kane, 33, was injured around 20 minutes into Bayern's 1-1 home draw with Cologne in their Bundesliga match on Friday.

Bayern issued a statement on Saturday saying that Kane had "successfully undergone surgery" on his left ankle but was expected to be out for three to four months.

England captain Kane, who finished the 2025–26 season with over 70 goals for club and country, was awarded the Ballon d'Or for his efforts.

Hubert Aiwanger, the deputy premier and economy minister of the southern state of Bavaria, is being buried on Saturday in his native town of Inkofen.

Aiwanger, the federal leader of the Free Voters (FW) party, died suddenly two weeks ago of natural causes at the age of 55 in a hotel in Berlin.

The funeral service ahead of the burial was open to the public, with police saying they expected some 1,000 participants.

A memorial service was held in Munich a week ago to honor Aiwanger.

We're amazed at just how much is loaded into this package for such a low price. It's surprisingly good quality, too, with the unit itself being sturdy and made out of hard-wearing plastic.

This isn't a scientific star projector, of course. For that, we'd recommend the Sega Toys Homestar Classic or the Hommkiety Galaxy Projector. But even though the YunLone Galaxy Projector won't give you an accurate view of the Northern Hemisphere's night sky or a close-up of the moon, it's still a projector we recommend. If you're looking to create a relaxing atmosphere, it's one of the best star projectors we've reviewed.

In a recent development, the YunLone Galaxy Projector doesn't have the most attractive design: It's clearly built for functionality rather than aesthetics. If an aesthetically pleasing projector unit is what you're looking for, perhaps consider the Jiawen Galaxy Projector Light. You won't find nearly as many functions as the YunLone Galaxy Projector packs in, however.

According to recent reports, that isn't to say that the YunLone Galaxy Projector is ugly, though. The design is basic, with a circular shape that houses a clear globe in the middle that acts as the projector. It sits on rubberized feet, so it doesn't easily slip or move around, and it's naturally tilted, so it points slightly diagonally rather than straight up. Given the wide reach of the projector, it helps spread the aurora lights across your entire room.

According to recent reports, the projector has a solid build quality: It's plastic but feels sturdy and well-made. If you're buying for a child's bedroom, you don't need to worry about little hands being too rough when using it. Those rubber feet help prevent it from being knocked off a desk or bedside table, too.

Sources indicate that as already mentioned, the YunLone Galaxy Projector isn't a scientific star projector. If you want to recreate actual constellations and close-ups of planets on your bedroom ceiling, this is not the projector for you. But if you're looking for beautiful, mesmerizing aurora-style patterns, it's a great choice.

Once you're connected to the app, you can control exactly what colors the projector displays. Not only can you choose from a number of preset arrangements — labeled as seasons, colors or holidays, so you can create a mood that matches the time of year or how you feel — but you can set your own entire color scheme by choosing from a color wheel. You can also set the brightness, whether the lights will have a "breathing" effect, and how fast they ripple across your ceiling.

In a recent development, it's a very neat touch, and it goes beyond what we'd expect to find in a star projector in this price range. If you don't want to bother with app connection, you can still set a range of colors and options from the remote control, but the options here are more limited.

According to recent reports, the YunLone Galaxy Projector comes equipped with a laser, so it can project green laser stars onto your walls and ceiling. We didn't love the look of these, though, so it's good that you can turn them off independently of the aurora lights. You can also change the laser's brightness if you'd like the stars to appear dimmer.

In a recent development, both the laser stars and the aurora projections have a very wide reach, covering most of the walls and ceiling of the bedroom we tested the unit in. Obviously, this will vary depending on the size of your room and how far away from the ceiling/wall you place the unit, but we were pleasantly surprised by the coverage offered by this projector.

The YunLone Galaxy Projector has a companion app that can be downloaded onto an Android or Apple smartphone. Once the app is set up and paired with your unit, you have full control over the colors, speed and brightness of your projections.

The pairing process isn't entirely straightforward, however, with no simple way of forcing the projector to enter pairing mode. The instructions tell you to promptly turn the unit on and off three times, but it took several attempts before we successfully put the projector into pairing mode.

Thankfully, once that's done, it should stay paired with your smartphone permanently so you won't have to repeat the process. And the app itself is very easy to use, working seamlessly to change the colors of the projection unit.

Recent findings suggest that the bundled remote control (which requires two AAA batteries, not included) is a little more complex than most, offering a range of buttons to control both the built-in speaker and the light itself. We'd highly recommend opting for the app option as it gives you much better control over the unit, but if your smartphone is unavailable, you can at least set basic color and speed with the remote.

Industry observers note that you can connect a music player to the projector via Bluetooth to play your own audio through its built-in speaker. The quality is decent rather than outstanding: It obviously doesn't match the sound of a specialist speaker, but it's as good as we'd expect any $28 speaker to be. It lacks the bass that music requires to sound "complete" but will be ideal for listening to audiobooks and podcasts.

In a neat touch, the YunLone Galaxy Projector also has eight built-in sound effects, including white noise, waves, lullabies and a storm, which some users may find relaxing and good to fall asleep to.

Recent findings suggest that we have been thoroughly impressed with what the YunLone Galaxy Projector offers. Its projections are beautiful auroras that dance across your ceiling, and the ability to fully customize the color and speed is something that we really didn't expect to find at a $28 price point.

It has been revealed that if you're on a budget and looking for a non-scientific projector to use to relax and unwind with, we really don't think you can find a better unit. If, however, you want something that offers more scientific projections, you'll need to look elsewhere.

Industry observers note that sega Toys' range of projectors, including the Homestar Flux and the Homestar Classic, is excellent but comes with a much bigger price tag. The Hommkiety Galaxy Projector is worth considering too, offering realistic projections but with a price tag closer to $50.

The good thing about these projectors is that they come with interchangeable discs, able to display various images of space. The Hommkiety Galaxy Projector has several discs in the box, but you'll need to buy extra discs for the Sega Toys range, so that’s an extra cost to factor in.

If she's not building with plastic bricks, playing a video game, or writing about doing either of those things, you should probably check she's still breathing. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Red, red, green — those are the party colors of the left-leaning coalition recently formed in the German state of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania. Now a Berlin-based agency wants to see the same alliance between the center-left Social Democrats, the socialist Left Party, and environmentalist Greens win the 2029 national elections.

According to recent reports, the Goodforces wants to help make that a reality with their campaign neunund20 (twenty-nine), taking its cue, in part, from the American left. The agency was set up in response to the rise of the far right across Europe.

Co-founder Patrick Haermeyer told DW that the campaign's aim is "to give people hope and an alternative narrative to: Things are getting worse and worse." He worked as an online organizer for the election team of Bernie Sanders in the US Democratic presidential primaries in 2016 and cites Sanders' "not me, us" campaign as an inspiration.

Neunund20 currently has two strategies: It provides digital space for short-form videos and social media content on political and social topics on Instagram, Tiktok, and Bluesky. At the same time, it tries to connect content creators, activists, NGOs, and political initiatives around shared "progressive" issues.

Recent findings suggest that people with a particular interest can click to get a link giving them access to archives of relevant social media material that they can then reshare. That feature is modelled on the campaign of New York's left-wing mayor Zohran Mamdani.

According to recent reports, and there are other projects. The Goodforces was recently involved in a tactical voting initiative in the September elections in the state of Saxony-Anhalt, intended to keep the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) from winning an absolute majority. Haermeyer says physical campaigns of that kind are necessary to provide essential "interim victories" en route to the next parliamentary elections.

Recent findings suggest that the Greens and the SPD, the two parties recommended by the app created by the organization, made it over the 5% hurdle and into parliament. The help that they received was declared by each party in the form of a €40,000 ($43,900) donation.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The agency sees itself as a kind of Super PAC, modeled on political organizations in the United States that collect money to carry out campaigns without directly supporting a single party or a special candidate.

For Christoph Bieber, political scientist at the University of Duisburg-Essen, the Goodforces is an interesting new type of player on Germany's political scene because it operates outside the country's political parties.

It has been revealed that but many of those parties are eyeing the development with disquiet. The far-left, populist, immigration skeptical Alliance for Social Justice and Economic Reason (BSW) criticized the Goodforces' intervention in Saxony-Anhalt, telling the newspaper FAZ that it was an "infantilizing, and perhaps even antidemocratic action." The neoliberal Free Democrats (FDP) called the tool "wrong and intentionally misleading." The FDP failed to clear the threshold, while the BSW only just squeaked in. The AfD gained 43% of the vote and its candidate may soon become Germany's first far-right state premier since the Nazi era.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Industry observers note that haermeyer set up the agency in 2024 along with Peter Jelinek, and both men previously worked for Green Party European Parliament member Michael Bloss. Ahead of that year's European elections, the EU's Green Deal began to come under increasing attack.

That year also ended with the collapse of Germany's first federal coalition between the SPD, Greens, and FDP, after much infighting and attacks from right-wing quarters.

In a recent development, "We noticed that more and more successes and freedoms that we had fought for were being reversed: Things like freedom of movement, border checks, and other things that were coming more and more under fire," Haermeyer told DW. "And we noticed that it was primarily democratic and progressive forces that were being drawn into defensive battles.".

The AfD, founded in 2013, already in the age of social media, has successfully targeted younger voters with in its online campaigns. But the older parties, in particular, have struggled. The Goodforces saw a need for support in the online environment and is now seeking to plug this gap.

Industry observers note that the social media accounts of the campaign neunund20 contain posts on domestic German topics, such as the current negotiations to form a red-red-green coalition government in Berlin, and the country's fresh military service law. They also highlight "wins" in Spain in the protests for affordable housing and for US Democrats in the midterms.

Industry observers note that haermeyer stresses that the problems the agency highlights are determined together with a wide range of grassroots organizations and activists. "The campaign is not agreed in conjunction with the SPD, the Left Party, and the Greens," he said.

Sources indicate that agency funding comes from commissions and small donations. Haermeyer indicates that contributions generally range from $20 to $50.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Bieber sees the emergence of non-party campaigning, long an accepted practice in the US, as a bid to compensate for the shortcomings of traditional parties.

"It is an omission of the parties," he mentioned. "For years they have been saying we have to modernize, we have to become more open and get away from rigid membership structures. There are legal regulations governing the organization of political parties in Germany, but perhaps it could be more flexible and open.".

The center-left and center-right major-tent parties have been in decline for decades. Membership of the SPD dropped from 943,000 in 1990 to some 348,000 at the end of 2025. Chancellor Friedrich Merz's Christian Democratic Union (CDU) has seen a fall from 750,000 to under 357,000.

Party membership is particularly low in former communist eastern Germany. Centrist parties have also struggled to attract younger voters. A report by the Deutsche Kinder und Jugendstiftung (German Children and Youth Foundation) showed that only 20% of young people felt their concerns were taken seriously in the 2025 German elections and that trust in parties was low.

In the United States, campaign financing comes predominantly from donations, and lobby groups can buy influence by contributing unlimited amounts to super PACs. In Germany, party funding comes, in part, from taxpayers and membership fees, and donations are capped. However, Bieber warns that whereas there are strict rules regarding the disclosure of donors to US Super PACs, these do not exist in Germany.

According to recent reports, the political scientist does not believe that US-style campaigning is going to take hold in Germany, but he does see potential dangers: "This could be a door opener to make others consider whether they want to go in this direction in the field of campaigning. And he added: "If it becomes rife, it could lead to a further devaluation of parties and their structures.".

In a recent development, nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang to its top job earlier this week, the four-time adulterer pledging he'd be "a better CEO the second time around." Many supporters applauded his return, including prominent figures such as U.S. president Donald Trump, Tesla's Elon Musk, and OpenAI's Sam Altman.

Now another fan has spoken up: Denny's. The diner chain has confirmed that a commemorative Nvidia plaque is back in place at its Silicon Valley location, underscoring Huang's return to grace.

In 1993, Nvidia co-founders Huang, Chris Malachowsky, and Curtis Priem met in the San Jose Denny's to discuss ideas for the chip that would lead them to launch their organization. Ten years later, Denny's erected a commemorative plaque in the booth they'd used.

According to recent reports, "The booth that launched a $1 trillion tech giant," the plaque read at the time. Nvidia's value has since climbed to over $4 trillion, though recent turmoil has caused significant fluctuation. "Congratulations, Nvidia! Who knew that an idea started here would change the world?" Recent findings suggest that after Huang resigned on Nov. 12, people were quick to notice that the Denny's plaque had mysteriously disappeared. Denny's swiftly reinstalled it the very next day, stating that the diner "has long been a place where people and ideas come together, and that history deserves to be preserved." The plaque now reads "the booth that introduced a multi-trillion-dollar organization," though it's unclear exactly when its text was updated.

Denny's has since issued a further statement, saying on Wednesday that it "couldn't be prouder of the history we share [with Nvidia].".

According to recent reports, "We put that plaque right back up where it belongs," Denny's wrote in an X post. "Jensen, your booth is waiting and the coffee's on. We're always open, 24/7.".

The tech giant has not stated how or why the plaque was removed in the first place, saying only that it had "learned the plaque marking that booth had come down.".

Amanda Yeo is an Assistant Editor at Mashable, covering entertainment, culture, tech, science, and social good. Based in Australia, she writes about everything from video games and K-pop to movies and gadgets.

#208343. 'All coming together' - Isak repaying Liverpool faith

'All coming together' - Isak repaying Liverpool faith

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (898 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways

  • By scoring twice against Club Brugge in the Champions League, Isak took his tally for the season to 10 - more than double his total for his first season at the Reds.
  • Of course, that campaign was disrupted; he had no pre-season because of his protracted Â£125m move from Newcastle and then suffered a broken leg in December.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Liverpool fans have needed to be patient to see the best of Alexander Isak after an injury-hit start to his career, but the striker is now proving the wait has been worth it.

By scoring twice against Club Brugge in the Champions League, Isak took his tally for the season to 10 - more than double his total for his first season at the Reds.

Of course, that campaign was disrupted; he had no pre-season because of his protracted Â£125m move from Newcastle and then suffered a broken leg in December.

But Isak is now in a hot streak of form, having scored four goals in his past four games for Liverpool.

Asked whether fans were now seeing his full capabilities, Isak told TNT Sports: "It is always difficult to say exactly where you are and how good you are but I can definitely say I feel good, I am in a good place and the team is in a good place which is the most important thing.

"Hopefully it just gets better.".

When Isak scored his opener against Club Brugge, it marked a sixth consecutive away game in which he has struck.

That meant he joined an exclusive club of just eight players to have achieved that feat, following in the footsteps of Dick Forshaw, Sam English, Gordon Hodgson, John Evans, John Aldridge, John Barnes and Mohamed Salah.

Isak has now scored the joint-most away goals across all competitions this season (eight â level with Erling Haaland).

His total is also already more than any Liverpool player managed away from home in the 2025-26 campaign (six by Cody Gakpo, Dominik Szoboszlai and Virgil van Dijk) and it is only November.

Isak looks to be brimming with confidence, exemplified by his second goal as he latched on to a pass from Alisson to go through one-on-one and then chipped a confident finish past the goalkeeper.

But for Andoni Iraola, Isak's performance offered much more than goals, the Liverpool manager also praising the striker's overall contribution.

"He is in a great moment right now," he stated.

"In the first half especially he helped us with the link up. In the second half it was more about defending a little lower.".

Alexander Isak scored twice against Club Brugge but also demonstrated a willingness to drop back and help link up Liverpool's play.

Former Liverpool defender Stephen Warnock agreed that Isak had shown he has more to his game than the goals.

"There were a lot of questions about Isak last year, about his price tag and what Liverpool paid for him," he stated.

"There were a lot of people saying he doesn't take people on, but now he looks fitter and looks sharper and we are starting to see the quick, nimble feet again that we saw at Newcastle, with his nice touches and link-up play.

"So we are starting to see a different side of him. My big question in this system would be - can he press? Can he close down, can he affect the game in the other way that Iraola likes to do? Now we are starting to see that.

"All of it is coming together, which is great for him.".

Isak and Wirtz in a 'good place' - Iraola.

It is not just Isak who is looking the part in the Liverpool attack.

Florian Wirtz continued his impressive run of form with a goal that means he now has eight goal contributions in his last five games for Liverpool and Germany.

"Both are now in a good place," Iraola mentioned of Wirtz and Isak.

"When the team overall is playing well and we are getting good results everything looks a little better.

"The vital part if they help the team to play well and get results. Alex and Florian right now are in a good moment.".

But the Liverpool attack as a whole is looking dangerous, regardless of who plays along with Isak and Wirtz.

In Wednesday's 3-0 win, it was Victor Munoz and Bradley Barcola who completed the front four, while in Sunday's 4-0 defeat of Manchester United it was Rio Ngumoha who played in Munoz's position.

"We have so many good players in our team," Wirtz told TNT Sports.

"Even when we can substitute some wingers, midfielders or strikers in the 60th minute or later it gives us a lot.

"It demonstrates how good our team is and it is notable for a top team to have a strong bench.".

Liverpool's win against Club Brugge was their seventh from their last 10 games across all competitions.

"I spoke to Wirtz at the weekend, after the [Manchester] United game, and we were talking about his form - and he remarked 'well it helps that the team are playing well'," Warnock added.

"It's true because if you try to influence a bad team or a team that's not playing well, then it is much harder.

"With a fitter Isak, Wirtz looks a better player because now he is playing balls in behind that Isak is getting to, and getting in on goal on the back of.

"It has a knock-on effect, which is obviously like Wirtz remarked, he is playing in a team which is better equipped to suit him.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

China Renaissance, a top dealmaker in the country’s tech industry, said it would suspend trading of its shares and delay the release of its annual results because it still can’t get in touch with its founder.

Recent findings suggest that bao Fan, 52, started the boutique investment bank in 2005 and has been unreachable since the middle of February, according to the company. Shares in China Renaissance have plunged since Bao went missing, at one point dropping as much as 50%.

China Renaissance said in late February that it had learned Bao was “cooperating in an investigation” being carried out by certain authorities in the country. It gave no other details.

Chinese media have reported Bao might be assisting in an investigation related to a former executive at China Renaissance.

Recent findings suggest that in a filing on Sunday, China Renaissance said auditors couldn’t complete their work or sign off on their report because of Bao’s absence. The board was also unable to give an estimate about when it would be able to approve its audited results for 2022 or dispatch its annual report by an April 30 deadline as required by Hong Kong’s listing rules.

Missing Chinese billionaire CEO assisting authorities in investigation, company notes.

Trading in the company’s shares was suspended from Monday as a result.

In a recent development, bao is known as a veteran dealmaker who works closely with top technology companies in China. He helped broker the 2015 merger between two of the country’s leading food delivery services, Meituan and Dianping. Today, the combined tech giant’s “super app” platform is ubiquitous in China.

His team has also invested in US-listed Chinese electric vehicle makers Nio (NIO) and Li Auto and helped Chinese internet giants Baidu (BIDU) and JD.com (JD) complete their secondary listings in Hong Kong.

Sources indicate that over the weekend, China’s top anti-graft watchdog launched an investigation into Liu Liange, former party secretary and chairman of Bank of China, according to a statement by the Central Commission for Discipline Inspection and the State Supervision Commission. The bank is state-owned and one of the country’s four biggest lenders.

Liu is suspected of “serious violations of discipline and law,” the statement stated. He is among the most senior financial executives targeted in a broader financial crackdown by President Xi Jinping.

In January, Wang Bin, former party chief and chairman of China Life Insurance, was charged by national-level prosecutors with taking bribes and hiding overseas savings.

— Michelle Toh contributed reporting.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • United Airlines on Monday remarked it had resolved a "widespread system outage" that briefly affected departing flights.
  • "We have resolved a technology issue that delayed flight departures," the airline said in a statement.
  • A United spokesperson mentioned there was no indication that the outage was a cyberattack.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

United Airlines on Monday remarked it had resolved a "widespread system outage" that briefly affected departing flights.

"We have resolved a technology issue that delayed flight departures," the airline said in a statement. "While some flights were delayed, there was no impact on flights in progress, or on United Express flights.

A United spokesperson mentioned there was no indication that the outage was a cyberattack.

The Air Line Pilots Association, which represents pilots for United and other carriers, noted in an earlier message to members seen by CNBC that the operational outage was "affecting multiple pilot facing applications" and that United could not "provide outbound flights with final weights.".

United's outage came three days after a nationwide ground stop halted departures across the country for more than four hours, snarling travel and leading to widespread delays and cancellations over the weekend.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy blamed the complications that led to Friday's ground stop on a router in Arkansas that overwhelmed systems that feed radar and other data for air traffic control. Federal Aviation Administration Administrator Bryan Bedford said the upgrades were part of "routine" maintenance to switch over from copper wires to fiber optic.

There were significantly fewer flight delays and cancellations Monday than had been reported Sunday, according to FlightAware data.

There was no indication that United's outage Monday was related to the issues that caused Friday's ground stop.

#208332. COP31 climate talks end without consensus on how to fund vulnerable countries or move the world away from coal, oil and gas use

COP31 climate talks end without consensus on how to fund vulnerable countries or move the world away from coal, oil and gas use

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1216 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Almost two days into overtime, climate talks in the Turkish city of Antalya have collapsed as countries led by the European Union rejected a deal that critics say undermines the shift away from planet-heating fossil fuels.
  • After two weeks of tough negotiations, the EU noted it could not support the proposed agreement, known as the Antalya Pact, put forward by the COP presidency, saying it does not respond to the science.
  • Sources indicate that "We will not endorse a cover decision that does not even mention fossil fuels, the driver of climate change.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Almost two days into overtime, climate talks in the Turkish city of Antalya have collapsed as countries led by the European Union rejected a deal that critics say undermines the shift away from planet-heating fossil fuels.

After two weeks of tough negotiations, the EU noted it could not support the proposed agreement, known as the Antalya Pact, put forward by the COP presidency, saying it does not respond to the science.

Sources indicate that "We will not endorse a cover decision that does not even mention fossil fuels, the driver of climate change. And we will not accept negotiating backward in time," said Irish climate minister Darragh O'Brien, speaking on behalf of the EU on Sunday.

He said adopting a decision that omitted fossil fuels would be "unconscionable" and risked "deepening the chasm between global commitment and the action required.".

Panama also rejected the deal, describing it as a step backwards in addressing the climate crisis, and adding that any decision must acknowledge "the truth about the collective failure on 1.5 degrees Celsius [2.7 degrees Fahrenheit]." That is the threshold outlined in the 2015 Paris Agreement to avert runaway climate change.

Industry observers note that "Those who contributed to this crisis ... must shoulder the responsibility to deal with it," the Panamanian delegation said.

According to recent reports, the Marshall Islands, which faces an existential threat from sea level rise, formally objected to the cover decision, saying "we will not compromise our future to benefit fossil fuel interests."   Chris ⁠Bowen, Australia's COP31 negotiating president ‌⁠stated the breakdown in talks was very ‌disappointing. Russia, however, supported the decision to leave out wording on accelerating a phaseout of fossil fuels, arguing that they are still a necessary power source and that each country should be able to determine its own pathway on how to cut emissions.

Industry observers note that pakistan and Ghana, defended the agreement as a necessary compromise in the spirit of multilateralism. "We need to build bridges not barriers," stated the Pakistan negotiator.

In a recent development, the marathon talks, held at a time when the window is rapidly closing to avoid the escalating impacts of climate change, including drought, deadly heat and flooding, also saw major disputes over financing. Developing states blamed the collapse in talks on the EU and other wealthier nations for failing to scale up financing to help them adapt to climate-linked weather extremes and the damage they cause. The EU is the largest provider of climate finance and has resisted new adaptation finance targets.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Harjeet Singh of the Fill the Fund campaign accused wealthy countries of demanding greater climate ambition while refusing to stump up the cash to pay for it.

"You can't ask developing countries to transform their economies while they're drowning in disasters and debt," he added.

The final cover decision had proposed further discussions on "an implementation pathway for tripling adaptation finance by 2035" but without mentioning a figure. It noted that developing countries need some $300 billion annually for adaptation until 2035, and expressed concern about "the gap between climate finance flows and needs.".

Outside formal negotiations, a separate initiative to Transition Away from Fossil Fuels (TAFF) has been gaining momentum.

Maina Talia, Tuvalu's minister for climate change and the environment, mentioned TAFF was "moving beyond debating whether fossil fuels are simply mentioned in a text, to creating detailed plans for a global transformation.".

At the same time, a growing number of states, including Ireland, Denmark, the Netherlands, France, Germany and Finland, have either completed or are working on so-called national roadmaps to wean themselves off fossil fuels. But Brandon Wu, director of Policy and Campaigns ActionAid USA, dismissed such plans as "meaningless" and "nothing more than restatements of inadequate existing policy" on the part of rich countries not stepping up on climate finance. "COP31 was one of the worst COPs ever, and it's because the EU and other developed countries came with zero spirit of solidarity, cooperation or compromise. They may as well have come to the COP shouting at vulnerable communities: 'we don't care if you die.'".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The rejected cover decision had recognized that electrification can deliver emissions reductions, improve energy security and expand access to energy.

Industry observers note that it included a call to increase the share of electricity in final energy demand from around 20% now to 35% by 2035 — a proposal heavily touted by co-host Turkey. Still, about 75 countries, including solar powerhouse China, adopted the pledge outside of the formal negotiations. It is non-binding and does not specify whether that additional electricity must come from clean sources. Critics say this leaves open the possibility that expanded electricity demand could be met by fossil fuels.

Sources indicate that the talks in Turkey marked the first time a COP was taking place under the explicit knowledge that global temperatures will exceed 1.5 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels. Countries were split on how to deal with that so-called "overshoot.".

The cover decision had called on states to commit to limiting overshoot , acknowledging that every increment of warming above current levels would "result in increasingly adverse, and in some cases irreversible, impacts and risks to human and natural systems.”.

It also recognized the need for "deep, rapid ​and ‌sustained" emissions cuts and for action on ramping down potent greenhouse gas methane.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Another contenious matter at the talks and in the final draft decision was a call for "increasing" carbon capture and storage technologies that entails capturing CO2 and burying it. The text noted the world should aim to reach "gigaton scale" by 2035.

In a recent development, scientists say some carbon removal technologies will be necessary to curb emissions and bring temperatures back down. But critics argue they are unproven at scale, expensive and risk giving polluters an excuse to keep burning fossil fuels.

Vanuatu's climate minister Ralph Regenvanu said carbon capture and storage "had been singled out for special attention that it doesn't deserve.".

Industry observers note that the stakes were high at COP31. The summit followed a string of recent climate-related disasters, from deadly heat waves in Europe to a glacier collapse in Nepal that killed more than 1,400 people.

At the same time, geopolitical shocks that sent oil prices rising globally shifted the focus onto energy security and the future of fossil fuels.

Speaking near the end of the conference in Antalya, Ethiopian foreign minister Gedion Timothewos, who will preside over COP32, mentioned his country aimed to "restore hope, rebuild trust and mobilize collective action" at the next summit to be held in 2027 in the Ethiopian capital Addis Ababa.

"We will work with you all to rebuild confidence in multilateral climate cooperation. This confidence must be earned through delivery. The decisions we take at COPs must advance climate action and implementation.".

With reporting from Tim Schauenberg and Katharina Schantz in Antalya.

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Space ↗ Open Full Page

1st-ever detection of a dying star's 'final nuclear heartbeat' challenges what we know about our sun's eventual death

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (915 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Space

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As ubiquitous as the sun is to us today, our star is not eternal; one day, albeit in billions of years, it will die.
  • Fresh observations collected using the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA), the world's largest radio telescope comprised of 66 antennas in northern Chile, reveal that the sun's death throes may be different from what scientists had initially believed.
  • According to recent reports, NASA Jet Propulsion Lab (JPL) researcher Raghvendra Sahai, who led the investigation, explained the shape the ALMA observations took: "It's essentially a physical snapshot of an event that, until now, we've mostly inferred from theoretical models.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As ubiquitous as the sun is to us today, our star is not eternal; one day, albeit in billions of years, it will die. While massive stars die in supernova explosions, the sun and stars of similar mass die quieter deaths. But that doesn't mean these stars completely go out with a whimper.

Fresh observations collected using the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA), the world's largest radio telescope comprised of 66 antennas in northern Chile, reveal that the sun's death throes may be different from what scientists had initially believed.

According to recent reports, NASA Jet Propulsion Lab (JPL) researcher Raghvendra Sahai, who led the investigation, explained the shape the ALMA observations took: "It's essentially a physical snapshot of an event that, until now, we've mostly inferred from theoretical models. We've caught, for the first time, a star's final nuclear heartbeat, frozen in gas.".

Sources indicate that sun-like stars "die" when they run out of hydrogen in their cores. This means that the fusion of hydrogen to helium ceases in the stellar core, and because this nuclear process is a star's main energy source, the star no longer has the outward push to support itself against the inward push of its own gravity.

According to recent reports, as the star's core collapses to create a stellar remnant called a white dwarf, the outer layers where hydrogen is still fusing to form helium swell out. This expansion leads to a relatively short-lived "red giant" phase. Eventually, these outer layers will cool and disperse, leaving the central white dwarf surrounded by a so-called "planetary nebula" shell of debris.

According to recent reports, during the red giant phase, as the stellar core is surrounded by shells of hydrogen and helium, these layers are occasionally rocked by flares in nuclear activity called thermal pulses. During these episodes, stellar material is flung into space.

To better understand this phase in stellar evolution, the team focused ALMA on a star called IRAS 06530-0213, located around 12,000 light-years away in the constellation Monoceros. This revealed a giant ring of gas that appears to be a frozen fossil of the star's last thermonuclear flare-up. This thermonuclear fossil rings an hourglass-shaped planetary nebula in the act of forming.

"Most of us think of stars as unchanging points of light, but this is a real-time snapshot of a star's death throes," Sahai said. "It's the brief, violent transition between a bloated red giant and a glowing planetary nebula, frozen mid-action.".

The team was able to determine that this gas shell of IRAS 06530-0213 is around half a light-year wide and was ejected into space around 6,500 years ago. It represents the first direct evidence of the last thermal pulse before this kind of star enters the final phase of its life.

In a recent development, the team thinks that for around 2,000 years after the pulse, the star lost mass at a lower rate. This mass loss then increased sharply over the following 1,000 years. This led to the creation of a lumpy shell of gas now seen as a tangle of material filaments around the dying star. The fact that these filaments have a spiral shape could indicate that IRAS 06530-0213 has an unseen partner orbiting it, stirring the gas.

Meanwhile, the hourglass-shaped nebula immediately around the star began to take shape around 700 years ago, meaning that the red giant phase for IRAS 06530-0213 only ended very recently, in cosmic terms at least.

There are also unexpected elements to the ALMA observations of IRAS 06530-0213.

The team discovered an unexpected abundance of heavy versions, or isotopes, of elements like carbon, oxygen and nitrogen around IRAS 06530-0213.

This doesn't conform to models of how stars like IRAS 06530-0213 forge elements and mix them into their surroundings, though similar signatures have been seen around odd stellar objects, with violent bursts of nuclear fusion thought to be the cause.As well as seeing something unexpected, the researchers didn't detect something they expected to observe.

Industry observers note that dying stars like IRAS 06530-0213 have previously been known to have companions, typically sitting with them inside compact disks of dust. These disks are indirect evidence of material being dragged from the close companion star to the dying star. This is a process scientists have used to explain jet-sculpted hourglass shapes.

However, ALMA failed to detect such disk around IRAS 06530. The team suggests that this could be because a disk existed, albeit briefly, during which time it powered a short burst of high-speed jets that helped sculpt the hourglass, following this the disk simply faded away.

Recent findings suggest that "Dying stars so often have hidden companions that reshape their ejected material into intricate, bipolar or multipolar forms instead of simple spheres," Sahai concluded. "IRAS 06530 shows that the story is more complicated than the tidy explanation we've been using."The team's research was published on Friday (Nov. 20) in The Astrophysical Journal.

Recent findings suggest that robert Lea is a science journalist in the U.K. whose articles have been published in Physics World, Fresh Scientist, Astronomy Magazine, All About Space, Newsweek and ZME Science. He also writes about science communication for Elsevier and the European Journal of Physics. Rob holds a bachelor of science degree in physics and astronomy from the U.K.’s Open University. Follow him on Twitter @sciencef1rst.

#208320. Latest Update: Rule-breaking is contagious — and good examples barely help

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (762 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dw ↗ Open Full Page

Latest Update: Rule-breaking is contagious — and good examples barely help

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (762 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that most people stop at a red light, even when the road is empty.
  • Industry observers note that A latest study suggests they become more likely to follow.
  • Industry observers note that A small number did more than copy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that most people stop at a red light, even when the road is empty. But what happens when the person next to them walks straight across?

Industry observers note that A latest study suggests they become more likely to follow. In an online experiment led by researchers at the University of Amsterdam, people who saw someone from their own political camp break a rule outright were nearly twice as likely to do the same. Seeing someone follow the rule barely made a difference.

Industry observers note that A small number did more than copy. They broke the rule by more than the person they had watched. According to Lucas Molleman, an assistant professor of developmental psychology at the University of Amsterdam who led the research, a few bad actors like these can "basically take off the guardrails of the group.".

It has been revealed that the researchers wanted to know how seeing other people's choices affects whether someone sticks to a rule. They recruited 750 adults in the United States, roughly half Democrats and half Republicans, a week before the 2024 presidential election.

Sources indicate that participants watched an animated shooting star cross a row of 100 squares and were told to click the square where it shone brightest, which was always near the middle. Squares further to the right paid more money, so there was a reason to cheat.

Each person chose first on their own. They were then shown what a previous participant had done, whether that person had followed the rule, bent it or broken it outright, and which party they supported. Then they could change their answer. The task was repeated six times.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The experiment had no real-world stakes, and nobody was punished for cheating. Other researchers say that matters. "That's not how the world works," Eugen Dimant, a behavioral economist at the University of Pennsylvania who was not involved in the study, told Science News.

Punishment and social pressure, he argued, also shape whether rule-breaking spreads.

Rule-breaking spread in the experiment. When people chose on their own, they picked the square furthest to the right, the most lucrative and most blatant violation, about 23% of the time. After seeing someone from their own party make that choice, they did so almost 40% of the time.

Small violations had only a small effect. Blatant ones had a much larger one.

Most people matched what they had seen or stayed below it. But just over 4% went further, breaking the rule by more than the person they had watched.

Sources indicate that good examples had little effect. Seeing a previous participant stick to the rule rarely changed what others did, even when that person was from their own party.

Industry observers note that people also differed. Some followed the rule every time and others broke it every time, whatever they saw. The rest shifted depending on what others had done.

It has been revealed that people were more likely to copy rule-breaking when it came from their own side. The effects were stronger when the person being watched shared the participant's political leanings.

Sources indicate that not everyone reads that as contagion. Stephen Reicher, a social psychologist at the University of St Andrews in Scotland who was not involved in the study, told The Guardian that if influence depends on who the other person is, it does not spread the way a disease does. He pointed out that people who see a riot often turn up afterwards to help clean up.

In a recent development, to see how individual choices might add up, the researchers ran computer simulations. They created a digital version of each participant and placed them in groups of 100.

In a recent development, in some scenarios, the handful of people prone to escalating pushed the whole group toward heavy rule-breaking. But when the simulated groups contained the same share of committed rule followers as the real experiment, rule-breaking leveled off at a moderate level.

Molleman called the work fundamental science and stated the real world is far more complex. He sees possible links to situations such as drivers speeding together, or protests that turn violent.

He also stated it challenges how people see themselves. In individualist cultures such as the Netherlands and the UK, he said people tend to believe they make their own decisions. But "in many, many cases we are very much influenced by what others are doing.".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Voting remains open for the BBC Men's Footballer of the Year 2026 award, which will be presented at Sports Personality of the Year.
  • Fans from the UK can vote from the five-player shortlist of Jude Bellingham, Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappe, Rodri and Lamine Yamal.
  • The vote closes on Friday, 27 November at 09:00 GMT.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Voting remains open for the BBC Men's Footballer of the Year 2026 award, which will be presented at Sports Personality of the Year.

Fans from the UK can vote from the five-player shortlist of Jude Bellingham, Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappe, Rodri and Lamine Yamal.

The vote closes on Friday, 27 November at 09:00 GMT.

The winner of the award - new for this year - will be presented during the live Sports Personality of the Year show on Sunday, 13 December.

Alex Kay-Jelski, Director of BBC Sport, said: "From the drama and excitement of the men's World Cup to the moments that have captivated fans across the domestic and international game, 2026 has given us so much to celebrate.

"Our inaugural BBC Men's Footballer of the Year award is about recognising the players who have made this year so special, inspired fans and left their mark on the game.

"It's a fantastic shortlist, and I can't wait to see who the public choose as our first-ever winner.".

The shortlist was selected by an expert panel comprising former international players and some of the BBC's most respected football voices, bringing together a wealth of experience and insight from across the game.

The panel included Cesar Azpilicueta (Spain), Scott Brown (Scotland), Olivier Giroud (France), Shay Given (Republic of Ireland), Hassan Kachloul (Morocco), Lucas Leiva (Brazil), Benni McCarthy (South Africa), Alan Shearer, Ellen White (both England) and Ashley Williams (Wales).

Read more on the five contenders and cast your vote below.

Sorry, this vote cannot be loaded. In order to vote you need to enable JavaScript in your browser.

Meet the SPOTY Men's Footballer of the Year contenders.

Club: Real Madrid Position: Midfield.

Bellingham made history this summer as he became the first Englishman to score as many as seven goals at a major tournament.

In a superb World Cup for the midfielder, he memorably netted twice in back-to-back games to help the Three Lions beat Mexico and Norway.

That meant he joined exalted company as the first player to score two or more goals in successive World Cup knockout games since Diego Maradona in 1986, and the second youngest in history behind Pele in 1958.

Bellingham also became the youngest European player to make an appearance at four different major tournaments, and also reached the milestone of 50 caps at a younger age than any other England men's player.

The goals continued to flow for Real Madrid, too, with Bellingham notching his 50th for the club to move above the legendary Zinedine Zidane in the Los Blancos' all-time scoring charts.

Bellingham was recently joined in the England squad by his brother Jobe.

Club: Bayern Munich Position: Forward.

In a stunning year of goalscoring, Kane become the first Englishman for 25 years (and only fifth in history) to win the Ballon d'Or - awarded to the world's best footballer.

His tally of 73 goals in 65 matches for club and country during a stellar 2025-26 season has only been surpassed in one of Europe's top five leagues by Lionel Messi's 82 for Barcelona and Argentina in 2011-12.

Recent findings suggest that kane scored 61 of those goals in just 51 appearances for Bayern Munich as he helped the Bavarians to a league and cup double. His total was 19 more than any other player in Europe's top five divisions.

Already England's record goalscorer, he surpassed Peter Shilton's mark of 125 appearances to become the most-capped Englishman in history.

Six goals at this summer's World Cup also helped him overtake Gary Lineker as the Three Lions' record scorer at the tournament, while he joined David Beckham as the only Englishmen to score in three separate World Cups.

Kane scored his first England goal 79 seconds into his debut in 2015.

Club: Real Madrid Position: Forward.

Mbappe came out on top of an enthralling tussle with Lionel Messi at the 2026 World Cup to become the leading goalscorer in the tournament's history.

The France forward, who is still only 27, took his tally to 22 from just three World Cups to finish one ahead of the great Argentine.

Mbappe's 10 goals from eight games this summer meant he won his second World Cup Golden Boot - a feat no player has managed before.

It also made him the first man to reach double figures at a World Cup since Gerd Muller in 1970, with only Just Fontaine (13) and Sandor Kocsis (11) having scored more goals in a single tournament.

Other achievements in a standout year included him finishing runner-up in the Ballon d'Or awards and overtaking Olivier Giroud as France's all-time leading goalscorer.

He scored 25 times to retain his title as La Liga's top scorer during a 2025-26 campaign in which he netted 42 goals in all competitions for Real Madrid.

Mbappe has won eight consecutive league golden boots.

Club: Barcelona Position: Midfield.

Midfield maestro Rodri earned yet another accolade in his incredible career when he was awarded the Golden Ball trophy for the World Cup's best player.

By captaining Spain to glory in the US, Rodri became only the fourth male player to win the World Cup, European Championship, Champions League and Ballon d'Or - following in the footsteps of legendary Germans Gerd Muller and Franz Beckenbauer and France's Zinedine Zidane.

His achievements were made all the more special given doubts remained over whether he would recapture his best form after a long recovery from a serious knee injury in 2024.

Recent findings suggest that then Manchester City boss Pep Guardiola predicted he would return to his best at the World Cup and he was right. Rodri completed 756 passes there - the most in the tournament since records began in 1966.

His final season at Manchester City before departing for Barcelona ended in familiar fashion with a domestic cup double taking his trophy haul with the club to 14.

Rodri scored the goal that won Manchester City the Champions League in 2023.

Club: Barcelona Position: Forward.

Lamine Yamal continues to rewrite the record books with his astonishing exploits for club and country.

Recent findings suggest that just days after his 19th birthday, the Spaniard became the youngest footballer to have played in - and won - both a World Cup and a European Championship. The only players younger than him to play in a World Cup final are Brazil's Pele in 1958 and Giuseppe Bergomi for Italy in 1982.

For the second year running, his performances led to a podium place at the Ballon d'Or and at the same award ceremony he became the first footballer in history to win the Young Talent of the Year three years in succession.

At club level, he was named La Liga's Best Player courtesy of a starring role in Barcelona's title success. The teenager ended the season with an impressive 24 goals and 18 assists across all competitions.

He recently broke Kylian Mbappe's record for the most goals by a teenager in Champions League history.

Lamine Yamal was 16 years and 362 days when he scored at the European Championship in 2024.
